full_text:
Andrew A. Loomis

Deputy Assistant Secretary of War for Russia, Ukraine, and Eurasia

|

 

Andrew Loomis is the Deputy Assistant Secretary of War for Russia, Ukraine, and Eurasia (RUE) in the Office of the Under Secretary of War for Policy.  He is responsible for the defense strategy and policy for countries in the RUE region.

Previously, he served as the Special Advisor for Europe and Russia in the Office of the Vice President, where he planned and prepared the Vice President’s meetings and travel in Europe and worked closely with the National Security Council to implement the White House’s foreign policy objectives in Europe. 

Andrew is a career Foreign Service Officer with the Department of State with experience working on Russia and NATO as well as overseas assignments in Rome, Kabul, and Santo Domingo.  Before joining the State Department, he worked in the energy industry and was an infantry and intelligence officer in the U.S. Marine Corps, with a deployment to Helmand Province, Afghanistan, as part of Operation Enduring Freedom.  Andrew graduated with a degree in Economics from the University of Texas at Austin and a law degree from The George Washington University Law School.

related.title: Saving Lives Under Threat: Thousands in Central Mali Protected from Explosive Risks Amid Funding Crisis (pdf)
related.summary: Thousands of civilians have been displaced in search of safety away from their communities and the impact of the insecurity across the Sahel has also resulted in large number of refugees seeking safety in Mali. Almost 55,000 Malians have received lifesaving training on identifying and deal with unexploded bombs – and now the same people are training others in their communities.
bullets: Thousands of civilians have been displaced in search of safety away from their communities and the impact of the insecurity across the Sahel has also resulted in large number of refugees seeking safety in Mali.
Almost 55,000 Malians have received lifesaving training on identifying and deal with unexploded bombs – and now the same people are training others in their communities.
According to the UN’s office for Humanitarian Affairs, OCHA, only 16% of the $577.9 million funding plan to help 5.1 million people in need of assistance in Mali in 2026 had been secured by May.
Mali is currently home to more than 138,000 refugees – predominantly from Burkina Faso and Niger.
They need support and protection – two things that DCA and its Malian partner AAPPOR (Association pour l’Appui aux Populations Rurales) have been delivering with EU humanitarian support.
related.excerpt: PRESS RELEASE “Saving Lives Under Threat: Thousands in Central Mali Protected from Explosive Risks Amid Funding Crisis” Bamako, July 14, 2026 While the number of displaced people in Mali is growing and funding is dwindling, DanChurchAid (DCA) Mali and its national partner, AA PPOR, continue to deliver support to tens of thousands of the most vulnerable among them with the support of the European Union. Almost 55,000 Malians have received lifesaving training on identifying and deal with unexploded bombs – and now the same people are training others in their communities. Mali has been impacted by the devolving security context in the Sahel for more than a decade – with grave human costs. Thousands of civilians have been displaced in search of safety away from their communities and the impact of the insecurity across the Sahel has also resulted in large number of refugees seeking safety in Mali. Mali is currently home to more than 138,000 refugees – predominantly from Burkina Faso and Niger. They are joined by a growing number of Malians who are displaced by fighting in their own country. According to the Malian government there were 378,363 internally displaced people (IDPs) in Mali
